title: New York Yankees vs. Seattle Mariners: Series Preview
description: The Yankees face a trident of right-handers as the scuffling Mariners dock in the Bronx.
fullText:
After three straight series against the Senior Circuit, the Yankees welcome the Mariners to the East Coast. The Bombers had an off day on Monday after dropping the series finale against the National League East-leading Atlanta Braves. The Yankees continue to hold serve as they wait for reinforcements to arrive, posting a 5-5 mark over their last 10 games, including an even 3-3 record thus far on the homestand.

The Mariners dock in New York after being swept at home by the pesky and, at this point, must-be-declared-legit Tampa Bay Rays. Seattle's season has not gone according to plan, as star catcher Cal Raleigh has struggled and the club enters play Tuesday sitting at 56-63. The Mariners have dropped four straight and are just 3-7 over their last 10 games.

This series features two night games before Thursday's getaway game, currently scheduled for 1:35 p.m. ET. Let's dive into which Mariners will be manning the harpoons and which Yankees white whales will be hoping to avoid the trident.

Tuesday: Ryan Weathers vs. Bryan Woo (7:05 pm ET)

Weathers has had a bit of an up-and-down first season in the Bronx. After opening the year looking solid, the month of June was not kind to the left-hander. However, since the calendar flipped to July, Weathers has found his footing again. Weathers currently has a 5-7 record, 3.79 ERA, and a 1.22 WHIP for the season.

Over his last three starts, he has thrown 18.2 innings while allowing just one earned run. That stretch includes six scoreless innings in his most recent outing against the Cardinals at home. Weathers has had his struggles in pinstripes this season, posting a 4.11 ERA at home compared to a 3.35 ERA on the road, but he will look to keep the ball in the yard and continue building on this recent momentum.

Woo is one of the best young pitchers in baseball, featuring a dominant four-seam fastball, excellent command, and the type of arm slot and tunneling that makes pitching nerds drool. The good news? Woo has been two very different pitchers this season.

At home, he owns an ace-like 7-0 record with a 1.96 ERA. On the road, however, Woo is 1-8 with a 6.71 ERA. That difference has held true recently as well. In his last two home starts, Woo has allowed just two earned runs across 13 innings. In his last two road starts, however, he has been roughed up for 10 earned runs in 10 innings. Those splits bring his overall season numbers to 8-8 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.12 WHIP. Expect Aaron Boone to send as many left-handed hitters to the plate as possible, as Woo's platoon splits also favor the lefties. Left-handed hitters have posted a .700 OPS against Woo this season compared to .585 from righties.

Wednesday: Will Warren vs. Bryce Miller (7:00 pm ET)

Much like Weathers, Warren has had his ups and downs throughout the 2026 season. Currently sitting at 8-6 with a 4.18 ERA, Warren's season has felt a bit like a roller coaster. After starting the year in dominant fashion, he has struggled as the weather has warmed. In July, Warren went 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA.

Warren has looked better in his last two starts. Against the Cubs, he tossed 6.2 scoreless innings, and in his most recent turn against the Cardinals, he allowed three runs over 5.1 innings. As one of the backend guys in this rotation, you have to expect some turbulence with Warren, take the good with the bad, and hope he can grind his way to a quality start.

The Mariners will send another power right-hander to the mound on Wednesday, as Miller gets the ball opposite Warren. On the season, Miller sits at 4-6 with a 3.08 ERA. He features an upper-90s fastball that he pairs with a nasty splitter and sweeper. Miller primarily uses the splitter to attack lefties and the sweeper against righties, and both pitches have been effective enough to produce almost identical platoon splits. Left-handed hitters have posted a .630 OPS against Miller compared to .629 from righties.

The good news for the Yankees is that, much like Woo, Miller has struggled away from the Pacific Northwest this season. At home, he owns a 2.09 ERA, while that number balloons to 4.02 on the road. More good news? The summer months have also been less kind to Miller, who currently finds himself in his worst stretch of the season. He has not made it through the sixth inning of a start since July 2nd.

Thursday: Max Fried vs. Logan Gilbert (1:35 pm ET)

The Yankees sandwich Warren with lefties as Fried takes the ball in the series finale. Fried has been steadily building himself back up after missing about two months of the season. Since returning, he has picked up right where he left off and currently owns a 4-3 record to go along with a tidy 2.88 ERA and 0.97 WHIP.

With two August starts under his belt, Fried looks ready for the postseason push. On the first of the month, he tossed 78 pitches of one-run ball against the Cubs before reaching 90 pitches while throwing 6.1 scoreless innings against his former club, the Braves, in his most recent start. I expect the training wheels to come off soon, and might I add that having a left-handed ace take the ball every fifth day is such an awesome thing to get to watch.

While the Yankees show a little spice of life on the mound, the Mariners roll out their third straight hard-throwing righty in Gilbert for the final game. Seattle's front office clearly has a type: tall right-handers who throw hard, get extension down the mound, and command all of their offerings. It is a good type, but with no real wrinkle from one day to the next, hopefully the Yankees' bats can lock in and light up Gilbert.

Gilbert owns an 8-7 record with a 3.42 ERA and 1.00 WHIP on the season. Unlike his other companions, Gilbert has actually been better on the road this year, posting a 2.50 ERA away from home compared to a 4.01 ERA at T-Mobile Park. In his most recent start against the Rays, Gilbert went 6.2 innings and took a tough 2-1 loss after allowing a pair of solo home runs that proved to be the difference. Tampa Bay also worked four walks, a season high for Gilbert.

The Yankees took two of three when they visited Seattle back in late March and early April. Here's hoping for more of the same this time around in the Bronx.

title: Meta glasses banned from courts in England and Wales
description:

fullText:
Exclusive: Court service says anyone trying to enter buildings with glasses will have them confiscated and returned when they leave

Courts in England and Wales have joined a number of restaurants, theatres and pubs in banning Meta glasses, amid a mounting backlash against what has been described as “spyware”.

Last month courts in New York announced a ban on the controversial glasses, which can record video footage while being worn.

Now His Majesty’s Courts & Tribunals Service (HMCTS), which is responsible for all criminal, civil and family courts in England and Wales, has made clear that Meta glasses will be confiscated from anyone entering its judicial buildings.

A spokesperson told the Guardian: “There are clear restrictions on taking images or videos within courts and tribunals which is why the use of Meta glasses is prohibited.”

Taking images or videos in court buildings is prohibited in the UK without official permission and can be prosecuted as contempt of court. While lawyers and members of the public are allowed to enter courts with smartphones, which can record both video and audio, the

HMCTS made clear that no such exception would be made for smart glasses.

A source said: “Users who bring Meta glasses into courts or tribunals will have them confiscated on entry and they will be returned when the owner leaves the building.”

They said smartphones were allowed on the condition they would not be used for recording court procedures.

Earlier this year, a claimant was accused by a judge of wearing smart glasses in the high court and getting “coaching” through them while giving evidence.

Laimonas Jakstys was told to remove the glasses during a case over the directorship of a property company. Raquel Agnello KC, sitting as a judge of the high court, said Jakstys had been “assisted or coached in his replies to questions put to him during cross examination”. Jakstys denied using the smart glasses to receive answers, and denied they were connected to his phone.

HMCTS does not hold figures on the number of incidents of smart glasses being used or taken into courts.

In February, members of the security team for Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, were seen wearing Meta glasses during a high-profile trial in California about social media addiction.

The judge, Carolyn B Kuhl, threatened the security guards with contempt of court if they had recorded any of the proceedings.

New York’s court system said it was banning smart glasses to ensure “individuals cannot surreptitiously record court proceedings”. It added: “No individual possessing smart glasses will be permitted to enter a UCS [unified court system] facility unless they voucher the smart glasses for safekeeping by uniformed personnel while the individual remains in the facility.”

Last year Meta sold 7m pairs of the glasses, which cost between £269 and £469.

Fears about Meta glasses being used to film people, especially women, without their consent has led to them being labelled “pervert glasses”. A number of restaurants, theatres and pubs in the UK, including Wetherspoons, have banned Meta glasses over privacy fears.

A spokesperson for Meta said the company did not want to comment on the court ban. They said when the glasses were recording a pulsing light was visible to people in the vicinity, and that frequently updated tamper detection technology is deployed to stop users covering this light during recordings.

title: New York Knicks reporter expects Karl-Anthony Towns to sign $45 million contract extension

Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win their first NBA championship in 53 years, playing elite defense against Victor Wembanyama throughout the NBA Finals.
fullText:
Despite not getting the $272 million supermax contract extension from the New York Knicks, Karl-Anthony Towns is likely to stay with the team.

Towns was instrumental in helping the Knicks win their first NBA championship in 53 years, playing elite defense against Victor Wembanyama throughout the NBA Finals.

And even though the Knicks aren't going to sign him to a lucrative long-term extension, the former All-Star is still expected to stay in New York on a more team-friendly contract.

New York Knicks beat reporter Ian Begley spoke about the future of Karl-Anthony Towns, who is unlikely to get the $272 million contract extension from the Knicks.

He noted that Towns and the Knicks have reason to extend their partnership, with KAT likely getting a $45 million per year contract offer.

"If I had to take a guess, the two sides will reach an agreement. Towns clearly loves New York. Maybe he can make more money with another team next summer (Towns has a $57 million salary this season and his contract has a $61 million player option for 2027-28).

"But why would he leave? He won a timeless championship with his hometown team. Unless the Knicks make an insultingly low offer to Towns, I think they get something done here.

"If I'm using the recent Rudy Gobert extension as a baseline, I could see an extension for Towns starting around $45 million."

Begley added that Towns could make more money as a free agent, but with the current financial restraints placed on teams due to the NBA salary cap rules, staying with the Knicks on a team-friendly deal is a far safer option for him.

"By signing this kind of deal, Towns would obviously lose the opportunity to make more money as a 2027 free agent.

"Given all of the factors at play (the state of NBA economics, teams' approach to the second apron, the Knicks' title), there are reasons for Towns to play it safe and sign an extension.

"Towns leaving New York also would hurt the Knicks. If Towns and the team can't agree on a deal, New York would have to make a significant pivot to find another front-line center. So from the outside looking in, it seems like it makes sense for both sides to figure out a deal."

It's hard to see the Knicks letting Karl-Anthony Towns walk in free agency. Despite all the criticism they received for trading for Towns in 2024, he has rewarded their investment with a championship win.

On top of that, he has become a much better defender than he was earlier in his career, thus providing the Knicks with an elite two-way big who can stretch the floor, an archetype incredibly rare in the modern NBA.

The Knicks know that they can't keep their championship core together for much longer, but they should maximise their time together for as long as possible.

title: Mamdani clashes with Democratic Socialists' push to abolish police and prisons
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended police, prisons and jails on air, distancing his administration from the DSA's abolition platform.
fullText:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended police, prisons and jails during a Friday appearance on "The Clay Cane Show," putting distance between his administration and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) platform as political streamer Steven Bonnell, known online as "Destiny," told Fox News Digital that Mamdani would likely govern moderately while helping more radical candidates gain power.

Bonnell said Mamdani's control of a prominent and politically secure office could allow him to build support for other socialist lawmakers without implementing the DSA's most radical proposals himself.

"I think that Mamdani holds a very powerful, very safe office where he can be entrenched for a long time in order to 'hold the door open' for other, (arguably) more radical lawmakers in the future," he said.

Harris Reaches Out To Socialist Mayor Mamdani In Latest Sign She's Shoring Up Support For Possible 2028 Bid

Mamdani addressed his differences with the DSA after host Clay Cane noted that the organization's platform calls for abolishing institutions including prisons, the Senate and the presidency.

"I would say, especially when it comes to public safety, I've been very clear that we have our police force, we have prisons, we have jails [and] the purpose of these is also to ensure that we are delivering safety and justice hand in hand. And what that means is that New Yorkers need not choose between the two," Mamdani said.

He also credited the NYPD with driving down violent crime while emphasizing that public safety should not come at the expense of justice.

"I am proud of our police department for their work in delivering the lowest levels of murders and shootings and even the number of shooting victims in recorded history over seven months over this year," Mamdani said.

Mamdani Walks Back Plan To Increase Nypd Headcount Following Dsa Pressure

The NYPD reported 381 shooting incidents, 462 shooting victims and 149 murders during the first seven months of 2026, the lowest record totals for that period. Major crime declined 6.6% compared with the same period in 2025.

The position contrasted with the DSA's official platform, which describes defunding law enforcement and weakening police unions as steps toward eliminating police and prisons.

DSA co-chair Megan Romer defended the organization's approach to police and prisons during an interview with New Yorker editor David Remnick Monday on "The New Yorker Radio Hour." Romer rejected eliminating law enforcement, while defining defunding as redirecting department money into social programs.

"I am not in favor of getting rid of police entirely tomorrow," Romer said. "I think it means taking funding back and moving it elsewhere, right?"

"It's not communities with cops on every corner. It's communities that have good schools, good jobs, good park systems, good recreation for their teenagers, things like that," she added.

Dsa Co-chair Pushes Back On Soviet Union Comparisons, Wants Prisons To Be 'Less Necessary'

Bonnell predicted to Fox News Digital that the demands of running the nation's largest city would keep Mamdani from applying the DSA's policies, even as the mayor used his popularity to promote other socialists.

"As someone who has to actually govern, though, I don't see him applying any of the more radical DSA positions," he said. "Rather, he'll govern moderately, remain decently popular, market well, then use that position and popularity to promote others."

Republican New York City Councilwoman Vickie Paladino's office told Fox News Digital that Mamdani's remarks were intended to obscure an agenda that remained central to the DSA.

"Mamdani is politically savvy and understands that DSA messaging on police and prison abolition has been embarrassing and deeply problematic for Democrat candidates heading into the midterms," Paladino said. "As the top DSA figure in the country, he's trying to deploy some smokescreen on behalf of the party, nothing more."

"Make no mistake, abolishing police and prisons is now a baseline policy position for the DSA, regardless of what Mamdani is saying at the moment," she added.

Despite distancing his administration from that platform, Mamdani praised NYC-DSA during the interview for helping elect minority candidates.

"And I think to me, one thing I've appreciated about New York City DSA is that it has been one of the engines behind the creation of a new generation of Black and Brown leadership, the likes [of which] we haven't seen in quite some time," he said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's office, the national DSA and NYC-DSA for comment on whether the mayor's position conflicts with the organization's platform, but did not immediately receive a response.

title: It’s a New York turnaround as Braves pop home to face Mets

fullText:
What a quirk of the MLB schedule: the Braves wrap up a seven-game homestand, go to New York to face the Yankees, then immediately pop back to start a six-game homestand, which begins with the other New York team. Yeesh. To make it slightly sillier, the Braves just visited the Mets before that seven-game homestand began.

At 52-67 despite the season's highest payroll, the Mets are… the Mets. That said, they're not playing terribly right now: 5-3 in August, and 7-7 in the post-All Star Break portion of July, which included a series win over the Braves. For the season, the Mets have largely been marred by being the Mets, rather than anything else. They have the league's third-biggest xwOBA underperformance and its fourth-biggest FIP underperformance. Put those together and it's hard to avoid a miserable season, even if your team is in the top in, say, both xwOBA and xFIP-. What's "changed" since the All-Star Break is a smaller-sample reversal of fortune — the Mets have a massive xwOBA overperformance and are outperforming both their FIP and xFIP. So, y'know, stuff to be aware of in the back of your noggin. The Braves are 4-6 against the Mets coming into this series, so they'll need to sweep 'em to avoid losing the season series to them for the first time since 2017.

On the hill to potentially aid in that endeavor will be Bryce Elder, who brings an 88 ERA-, 108 FIP-, and 99 xFIP- (1.3 fWAR in 126 2/3 innings) to the proverbial table. Elder is in the midst of a silly run over his last four starts, as he's allowed four homers and has a 45/121/105 line in that span — the Braves have won three of those games. Overall, Elder's season has been about inconsistent as his game-to-game slider command. He started out pitching well, but the summer saw a decrease in performance with an especially-large uptick in the rate of homers yielded. One of those clunkers came in his only start against the Mets this year, which was one of his worst: a 2/2 K/BB ratio and two homers allowed in four innings, with the Braves getting blown out.

A random fact: Elder hasn't had a start with an ERA, FIP, and xFIP below 4.00 since May 16… though in terms of ERA, FIP, and xFIP each, he's had six, three, and four starts below that mark, respectively, since that May 16 date.

Opposing Elder for the Mets will be Christian Scott, who is having a nice season at 71/81/89 (1.7 fWAR in just 74 1/3 innings). He's been consistently strong all year aside from a disastrous season debut. The Braves did rough him up a bit in early July (two homers, a 7/4 K/BB ratio in four innings), but he dominated them a couple of weeks ago in New York (7/1 K/BB ratio in six innings), only for the Mets to lose that game as the Braves avoided a sweep behind Chris Sale. Scott has struck out five or more batters in eight straight starts, and hasn't allowed a homer in his last five outings. In fact, of the seven homers hit off him all season, six came in a three-game stretch.

title: Mamdani: Democratic socialists ‘going back to what the party used to be’
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said democratic socialists running as Democrats are “going back to what the party used to be.” Mamdani was interviewed for a pre-taped episode of the SiriusXM sh...
fullText:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said democratic socialists running as Democrats are "going back to what the party used to be."

Mamdani was interviewed for a pre-taped episode of the SiriusXM show "Urban View" on Friday. Host Clay Cane asked the mayor if he thinks there are any good contenders for the Democratic nomination for president in 2028. Both Cane and Mamdani dismissed the mayor as an option, as he was born in Uganda.

"I think we have a number of choices," Mamdani said. "I know that people are making their own choices, of whether or not they want to run. What I'm hopeful of is we're seeing a lot of examples of what it can look like to have that focus on the working person. People who understand that affordability isn't just something you say, it's something you have to deliver."

"And that in doing this, we're not running away from the Democratic Party; we're going back to what the party used to be. You think about FDR and La Guardia, you think about the New Deal; that's what the Democratic Party once was," Mamdani continued, referring to former President Franklin D. Roosevelt and former New York City Mayor Fiorello La Guardia (D). "That's what it could be again. And if we want to win, I think that's what we have to become."

Roosevelt and La Guardia led their respective reform agendas to enact New Deal policies aimed at lifting Americans in need of affordable healthcare and housing and facing poverty during the Great Depression of the late 1920s and early 1930s. Both championed policies that Mamdani said on the campaign trail that he would strive toward as mayor.

Such reforms are also popular among democratic socialists who have won a series of recent Democratic primary nominations on the heels of the mayor's victory last year. The victories have put a spotlight on divisions within the party over various policies, including Israel and the acceptance of political contributions from corporations and other political interests.

Democratic strategist James Carville, who notably worked on former President Clinton's 1992 campaign, has been an outspoken critic of the economic populist wave within the Democratic Party. He argued last week to CNN that the party's progressive left is "too hotheaded to know that they're not popular."

Some progressives, however, have dismissed Carville's summation of them and their effect on the party. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), who has been the target of some of Carville's remarks, said last week that there was not "much of a choice" with what Carville was saying.

"If Mr. Carville doesn't want to be in my party, the party I belong to, that Piker, that El-Sayed belongs to, he can start his own party," Sanders said, referring to Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) and popular left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker.

title: Survey results: Giants fans are feeling the optimism
description: Are NY Giants fans right to be optimistic about their team?
fullText:
The summer is the season for optimism around the NFL, the time when fans of every team allow themselves to indulge in hope for the coming season.

The New York Giants have had a bit more than a week of training camp and are about a week away from their first preseason game on August 15th. Rather than asking about anything specific before seeing the team on the field in a live situation, we wanted to take the temperature of the fanbase as things start to ramp up.

It isn't much of a surprise that the overwhelming majority of Giants fans are either optimistic, or outright excited, about their team. That flies in the face of the national perspective, where the Giants are an afterthought and even outright derided. Even Las Vegas views the Giants as extreme long-shots to make the playoffs this year, with the second-longest odds in the NFC, per FanDuel.

We'll see if the fans or the national perspective is right, but so far the news out of camp has been almost universally positive.

Camp under John Harbaugh has been faster and tougher than what we've seen in recent years from the Giants, with a much higher level of accountability.

The defense under Dennard Wilson has been consistently disruptive and at times dominant. The pass rush has been making the quarterbacks' lives difficult while the secondary hasn't been giving up much separation at all. And while they aren't hauling in all their interception opportunities, the defensive backs seem to be playing faster and more confidently than we saw the last two years.

The defense hasn't been allowing the offense to establish much rhythm or consistency, but we're still getting positive reports out of that side of the ball as well.

Both WR Malik Nabers and RB Cam Skattebo are healthier than many of us on the outside anticipated, and Odell Beckham Jr. has been rounding into form with increased reps. Rookie WR Malachi Fields has produced highlight reel catches with regularity, and the offensive line has looked good as well — despite the pass rush consistently getting into the backfield. It seems that's just a function of the Giants' hyper-athletic front seven, not poor play on the part of the blockers.

There are, of course, fans who aren't drinking the Big Blue kool-aid just yet — And that's fair. After all, the Giants looked amazing in camp and preseason last year, but still managed to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory on five separate occasions during the season.

We'll see how the good reports translate into the preseason, as well as how the Giants progress over their three preseason games. Last year there were consistent lapses in execution and assignment discipline that were never resolved and became the team's Achilles heel in the season. Even if the Giants don't win their preseason games, we'll see a solid baseline of execution and what issues that crop up be corrected.

title: Amazon responds to Mamdani’s cease-and-desist letter
description: Amazon has responded to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's cease-and-desist letters that went out to 40 major retailers over the sale of "prohibited motorized scooters and e-bikes."
fullText:
NEW YORK (WPIX) – Amazon has responded to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's cease-and-desist letters that went out to 40 major retailers over the sale of "prohibited motorized scooters and e-bikes."

Online retailers, including Wayfair, Walmart, Temu, Target and Amazon, were sent cease-and-desist letters demanding that the stores "immediately end the sale of" prohibited scooters and e-bikes to New York City residents and businesses, according to Mamdani.

If not, the stores could face $2,000 fines as of Aug. 18, Mamdani said Wednesday.

The prohibited nature of these scooters and e-bikes stems from the fact that some of the retailers' products exceed the legal speed limits and wattage limits. Some mopeds don't have proper VINs as well.

The speed limit for e-bikes in New York City is 15 mph. The maximum speed allowance must be under 20 to 25 mph, depending on the bike. Scooters can't weigh more than 100 pounds or go more than 20 mph.

"Let's be clear, these are motorcycles being marketed to New Yorkers as bicycles," said Department of Transportation Commissioner Mike Flynn.

The actions come a week after 17-year-old Gabriel Nacato was fatally struck by an SUV while riding an e-bike in Lower Manhattan. He was on his way from Bensonhurst to fill out summer job applications with a career counselor, Mamdani said.

"The vehicle he was riding is capable of reaching more than 30 miles per hour, a speed that should never be reached in our bike lanes," Mamdani said.

A spokesperson for Amazon told Nexstar's WPIX that the trillion-dollar corporation will be "looking into the products in question" and has no issue working with the mayor and City Council to get it right.

"Safety is a top priority and we require e-bikes sold in our store to meet applicable safety standards and Amazon policies," the spokesperson said.

Target has yet to respond to WPIX's request for comment on the matter.

fullText:
The New York Giants faced a bit of a scare at Friday's training camp practice when several players got banged up during live scrimmages and drills, including second-year running back Cam Skattebo.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan, who is in attendance at camp in West Virginia, shared details on Skattebo, center John Michael Schmitz, and edge Brian Burns.

"RB Cam Skattebo went down after a collision with LB Arvell Reese. He was stretching his left leg and didn't return to practice but remained on sideline," wrote Raanan.

"C John Michael Schmitz walked off early in practice after taking hard hit. OLB Brian Burns also got banged up but didn't appear serious."

While you never want to see players get hurt, especially before the season even begins, Giants fans can take a deep breath as it appears all of the aforementioned players will be okay.

After practice, New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh gave a brief update on Skattebo, Schmitz, and Burns, and reiterated that nobody was seriously harmed at Friday's practice.

"John Harbaugh said JMS hit his head/got his bell rung. Skattebo just part of working back from last year's injury but nothing serious. Brian Burns played some but is managing an ankle," wrote the New York Daily News' Pat Leonard.

It's certainly a good update that no Giant will be missing any major practice time in the coming weeks, as all three players will be key starters for New York in 2026.

Skattebo in particular seems to still be getting reacclimated to the speed of the NFL. After all, he missed the second half of his rookie season and will likely need some reps throughout camp and the preseason to be 100% ready for Week 1.

If there's one positive thing New York Giants fans can take away from Skattebo's near-injury, it's the fact that it came on a monstrous play from first-round rookie Arvell Reese.

NorthJersey.com's Art Stapleton detailed the series of events in a post on X.

"Arvell Reese is the total package. Brings it old school. Popped Cam Skattebo in a run fit + the oohs/aahs were audible," wrote Stapleton.

"Next play Reese ran down Skatt from back side behind line. Skatt was slow to get up. Did a lot of stretching on side before walking across to other sideline."

One constant throughout Giants training camp thus far has been the emergence of Reese and how fast he seems to be adapting to the high-level of the NFL.

The fifth overall pick in this past April's draft, the former Ohio State standout figures to wear multiple hats for the Giants defense this upcoming season.

It seems he'll primarily serve as a weakside linebacker, serving as the sidekick to Tremaine Edmunds.

But thanks to his special physical abilities, there will be instances where new defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson will be able to send him as a pass rusher, an area he thrived at in college.

Let's just hope he refrains from laying the boom on any more Giants teammates.

fullText:
NEW YORK — It sounds like Carlos Rodón will rejoin the Yankees' rotation soon.

The southpaw, out with elbow inflammation since June 30, is scheduled to make his first rehab start at Triple-A on Saturday. The plan is for Rodón to throw close to 50 pitches for the RailRiders.

From there, Rodón may or may not make one more rehab start, manager Aaron Boone said Friday. Either way, the Yankees will activate the pitcher before he's fully built up and "definitely probably piggyback him" in his initial starts, Boone said.

With a number of off days on the upcoming schedule and five healthy starters already in their rotation, the Yankees should be able to make that strategy work without taxing their bullpen. The long-held assumption has been that the Bombers will move Ryan Weathers or Will Warren to the pen anyway once Rodón returns, so either could be the piggyback pitcher while staying stretched out in this scenario.

Rodón, 33, went 4-2 with a 3.30 ERA over nine starts before going back on the IL.

He initially hoped to miss minimal time due to the inflammation, but he's been out over a month now. He said that multiple rounds of shots — he's gotten PRP and orthovisc injections — are to blame for the prolonged timeline.

"I always try to get back as quick as I can," Rodón said Friday. "I feel like anybody in this situation would. I wouldn't say anything delayed me. We just had a plan with the injections, and when you're scheduling injections and trying to throw in between them, it kind of makes it harder to figure out when you can throw, when you can't. Because when you get an injection, you might need a day off. Obviously, you take the first day off. You might need a couple more days.

So obviously, I would love to be pitching for our team right now. But right now, it's just building pitch count and getting in games, and that's it."

title: These NYC centers allow hard drug use in-house. Nearly 5 years in, is it helping?
description: An addiction-services nonprofit approved by the city focuses on harm reduction for hard drug users — to the chagrin of some in the neighborhood.
fullText:
In a back room behind a colorful facade in northern Manhattan, drug users are smoking crack while nearby cubicles stand ready for heroin users to wrap tourniquets around their arms and inject themselves with new, sterilized needles.

It's all part of a 5-year-old experiment sanctioned by the city of New York, but not by the federal government, which has long-standing anti-"crack house" laws criminalizing facilities that allow for drug use.

Supporters say the supervised drug-use sites reduce overdose deaths and street drug use, and serve as a model for the rest of the country. But critics say the centers are magnets for hard drug users and dealers, leaving the local community feeling less safe.

"It's scary for the kids walking into school in the morning, seeing people in that state," said an educator at a nearby school who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.

New York City has two facilities like this, known as overdose prevention centers, or OPCs. By supervising the use of addictive, illegal drugs, proponents say the sites remove barriers to healthcare and can lead to people getting off drugs or transitioning to less risky behaviors.

In a recent interview with CBS News, OnPoint NYC Executive Director Sam Rivera said his team has intervened in more than 2,100 overdoses with no fatalities, and has more than 7,000 registered participants who have used the facility's services 250,000 times since it opened in 2021.

"250,000 times people used inside with us, not in the parks, not in the street, not in the playgrounds, not in bathrooms," said Rivera.

Rivera gave CBS News a tour of OnPoint's facility in East Harlem, a neighborhood where problems with drug use have persisted for decades.

In addition to the smoking room and injection cubicles, OnPoint offers services such as primary medical care, addiction medication, art therapy, sleep rooms and laundry, as well as perks like massage, acupuncture, aromatherapy and, soon, hair styling.

They are amenities that might seem more at home in an upscale wellness center than a place where people can inject heroin just a few steps from the massage tables. But Rivera said the wellness therapies serve a purpose.

"Those things are medicine. Those things are reducing drug use, introducing people into an environment that loves them," he told CBS News. "Many of our folks haven't experienced that."

In the massage room, an OnPoint participant-turned-part-time employee said, "I did the acupuncture, for the first time my back feels better. I didn't believe it but it really works."

Outside of OnPoint's walls, however, some residents say they're not happy about what it means for their neighborhood.

"You couldn't pay me to walk down that street anymore," said Syderia Asberry-Chresfield, co-founder of the Greater Harlem Coalition. "The dealers don't even have to look for clients. Drugs are being sold in front of everyone's faces. It's a slap in the face."

CBS News met Led Black, founder of the local media organization Uptown Collective, who lives a few blocks away from another OnPoint location in Washington Heights.

"I have three daughters. They're not little, but they're still young, they still shouldn't have to deal with this," he said. "You don't want the kids downtown to see it. Why is it OK for the kids up here to see it?"

In a campaign ad, New York state attorney general candidate Saritha Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor running as a Republican, singled out OnPoint as an example of bad policy.

"The problem here is these sites take people in, they give them deadly drugs, and then they turn them right back out on the street and into the subways. That's not a solution," Komatireddy told CBS News. "I think it's unethical. I think it's cruel, and it's definitely illegal." (OnPoint has a space for users to stay indoors and be monitored while they are under the influence of drugs.)

She notes that the East Harlem location is directly across the street from an early childhood development center and two blocks down from a school with students in kindergarten through grade 12.

Last year, Rep. Nicole Malliotakis, a New York Republican, publicly asked then-Attorney General Pam Bondi to shut down the facility, citing federal law prohibiting illegal drugs.

"They're enabling addiction instead of actually getting people the treatment they need to get off drugs," Malliotakis told CBS News. "They're also letting dealers know where their clients are."

In the 1970s, amid rising drug use in America, a movement began that would evolve into what's known today as "harm reduction" policy, with a core principle of removing any judgment or coercion from drug treatment.

Providing clean needles and testing drugs for contaminants that can cause sudden death seemed like the humane way to address painful-to-kick addictions, keep people alive, and reduce infectious diseases.

Despite the compassion behind the policies, they were no match for the nation's growing addiction crisis or increasingly lethal drug supply in recent years. Federal data show the rate of drug overdose deaths quadrupled in the U.S. between 2002 and 2022, a problem largely driven by prescription opioid pills before ballooning into a full-blown opioid epidemic.

Overdose deaths climbed to a peak of almost 108,000 in 2022 before starting to decline, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Overdose prevention centers that supervise drug use in-house are an extension of the harm reduction approach. While still unfamiliar to most Americans, they've existed internationally for two decades, with one report finding more than 100 such facilities worldwide, including many across Europe.

The one in Vancouver, Canada, is probably the most well known and has been in operation since 2003. Vancouver saw a steady rise in overdose deaths until a peak in 2022.

Just two months after taking office, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani visited OnPoint to show support for the program.

"This weekend, the team at OnPoint NYC kept their doors open 24/7 so vulnerable New Yorkers had somewhere safe to go," Mamdani posted on X  in March, alongside photos of himself with Rivera and other staff.

OnPoint operates with about $19 million in annual funding from a mixture of city, state and private funds, including some opioid settlement money. The city of New York funds a lot of it through multi-year contracts worth about $17 million in total. However, city rules prohibit using any of those funds for the direct supervision of drug use, so the organization has to rely on other sources for that work.

OnPoint once had more than $2 million in grants from SAMHSA, the federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, which it lost after President Trump issued an executive order in July 2025 explicitly barring federal taxpayer dollars from funding "drug injection sites" or "illicit drug use."

Despite the belief among many city officials, public health practitioners and researchers studying the programs that overdose prevention facilities are effective and necessary, their future in America is far from certain.

Efforts to open similar facilities in Seattle, Portland, San Francisco and Chicago have all failed. (Those cities have other harm reduction programs, such as needle exchange programs and social services for drug users.) Only Rhode Island has been able to move forward providing supervised drug consumption since OnPoint opened in 2021.

Rivera said he still wants to expand and has a community of city officials who support the notion.

The NIH's National Institute on Drug Abuse writes that after 20 years of international experience, "it is unclear whether such facilities reduce overdose death rates overall."

Existing studies tend to show some reduced death rates near the facilities that become hard to detect in larger populations. One systematic study from 2021 of existing international research concluded that OPCs "may help reduce overdose morbidity" while another study of Canadian programs across British Columbia found "no evidence that they reduce local hospitalization or mortality rates."

New York City's experiment with supervised drug use has been running for nearly five years — enough to start drawing conclusions about its impact.

Over the past two years, overdose deaths citywide have been decreasing rapidly from the highest recorded year ever in 2023, which tracks with the national trend. The city's Department of Health did not name OnPoint directly, but in a press release touting harm-reduction programs, it credited the change to "several years of increased investment in evidence-based overdose prevention strategies in NYC."

The NIH is now funding a team of researchers to evaluate America's three supervised injection sites: the two OnPoint NYC facilities and a newer one in Providence, Rhode Island, called Project Weber/RENEW. The multi-year study is still ongoing, and while they have not drawn conclusions on mortality rates, one of the lead authors said in an interview with CBS News that he believes overdose prevention centers have had a positive effect on public health.

Charles Fain Lehman looks at the very same data and sees a net negative. He is a senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute for Policy Research, a conservative think tank that has been a vocal critic of Mamdani's policies.

"There is a lot of evidence that interventions of this type generally do not have an appreciable effect on overdose deaths," Lehman told CBS News. "There's a fixed pool of resources available for helping people who are dealing with substance use disorder. If you're spending the dollars on an intervention that doesn't work, like supervised consumption sites … you're not spending dollars on [addiction medication] and evidence-based treatment."

A CBS News analysis of available crime data told two different stories between the two neighborhoods where OnPoint operates.

Felony crime complaints have risen steadily in the 34th Precinct, where the Washington Heights facility is located, since OnPoint opened in 2021. The precinct includes multiple city blocks, so the increase in felony crime complaints cannot be tied directly to OnPoint. Citywide complaints have also increased over most of that time, but more slowly than in the 34th.

In the 25th Precinct, where the East Harlem facility is located, felony complaints rose after 2019 and peaked in 2023. By 2025, felony complaints fell substantially but remained 10% above their pre-pandemic levels. The rest of the city fared worse, with felony complaints remaining near 2024 levels last year.

A CBS News review of 911 call data from the New York City Police Department showed most of the calls made from the OnPoint addresses were for ambulance services; relatively few calls required police response.

So far this year there have been 124 calls from the East Harlem location and 84 calls from the Washington Heights address.

A study in 2023 found no significant changes near the sites in "crime or disorder," which included 911 calls for trespass and 311 complaints.

Another study in the Journal for Experimental Criminology found a significant increase in property crimes near the Washington Heights location, where a Target store had recently opened. The study authors reasoned that placing the safe injection facility so near a location with easily shoplifted products created an environment ripe for theft. Notably, the study found no similar increase near the East Harlem facility and no increase in violent crimes in either location.

"This is our major conclusion, is that your location matters," said the study's co-author John Hall, a retired NYPD officer who is currently a PhD candidate at the Institute of Criminology at Cambridge University in England.

The NIH study's initial findings show that the sites seem to have a largely neutral effect on local business activity and drug-related criminal activity in their neighborhoods.

Brandon Marshall, one of the researchers on the NIH team evaluating America's overdose prevention centers, said, "OPCs can do many things. They can reduce public drug use, they can reduce 911 calls. They can help people access healthcare and treatment. They are not a panacea to all social problems in a neighborhood."

When the multi-year evaluation comes in from the NIH, it may move the debate about supervised drug consumption forward — or it may not.

Johns Hopkins bioethicist Travis Rieder argues that support for places like OnPoint will never be decided solely by the empirical data.

"I don't actually think it's why anyone believes what they believe," he said. "They have a view about what we should actually be helping people to do or not do, and then they find the evidence that best supports their view."

Rieder said he knows where he stands. "Here's what an overdose prevention site does: It says, 'You are welcome here, and I will watch over you so that you don't die today, and you're worth that. You deserve that because you're a human being and you have dignity.' And I think that's a really beautiful thing."

Black, the community activist, says he wants the researchers at universities studying OnPoint to spend a day in his shoes.

"Why should it be an addict-focused approach?" Black said. "I wish it were a community-focused approach."

–Jamie Korenblat and Max Moore contributed reporting.

title: Mamdani repeatedly sidesteps questions on reported plan to revive tax hikes on wealthy New Yorkers
description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani repeatedly declined to address reports of a fall campaign to build support for higher taxes on wealthy residents and corporations.
fullText:
New York City democratic socialist Mayor Zohran Mamdani repeatedly sidestepped questions Thursday about reported plans to launch a public pressure campaign this fall pushing tax hikes on wealthy New Yorkers and corporations.

Mamdani reportedly plans to build public support after Labor Day for similar proposals that Gov. Kathy Hochul previously rejected in early 2026. The reported push is expected ahead of the New York Legislature's return to Albany in January 2027 and Hochul's re-election campaign this fall, according to The New York Post.

During an interview with Fox 5 New York, Mamdani repeatedly declined to answer questions about the potential campaign before later saying such discussions would only come after the November election.

Asked whether he had spoken with Hochul about the reported campaign, Mamdani did not answer directly, instead using the opportunity to tout the opening of 2,000 free child care seats for New Yorkers through their policy efforts.

Nyc Mayor Mamdani Calls Threat Of Rich People Leaving Nyc Over Taxes 'Imagined'

"The governor and I are in constant communication and, frankly, I appreciate her partnership because if it wasn't for the governor, then we wouldn't have been able to stand together to announce that we had more than 5,000 New Yorkers come forward to apply for these 2,000 free child care seats," he said. "And I'm so excited about that, and the fact that we're going to expand to 12,000, and the work that's still to come."

The reporter then pressed Mamdani on whether the Democratic Socialists of America would join the potential campaign this fall, but he again declined to answer directly, saying his focus remains on the present.

Bernie Sanders, Dsa Reveal Demands For Dem Party After Socialists Sweep New York Elections

"My focus right now is where we are, which is August, and ensuring that everything that we're doing is keeping New Yorkers safe amidst a heat wave and preparing for the school year," Mamdani said. "A lot of the conversation about what comes after November, I think, is a conversation for what comes after November."

"So you don't plan to launch a campaign to tax the rich before the November election?" the reporter asked.

"The conversations I've been having with the governor and with my team are about the here and now and there will always be time for the conversations that come after that," Mamdani said.

Mamdani Extends Deadline For Nyc Homeowners To Seek Exemption From New Pied-à-terre Tax

The reported campaign would revive a previous push by Mamdani to close the city's multibillion-dollar budget gap through tax increases, a proposal Hochul previously rejected. Mamdani's earlier plan called for raising the city's personal income tax rate on filers earning $1 million or more, a move he projected could generate roughly $3 billion annually, while also increasing corporate tax rates.

As an alternative, Hochul and Mamdani jointly advanced the state's first pied-à-terre tax, an annual surcharge on certain high-value second homes, which passed in May 2026. State and city officials have projected the measure could raise about $500 million annually.

Mamdani also said his May 2026 executive budget closed what his administration described as an inherited $12 billion budget gap, crediting aggressive savings, new investments, his partnership with Albany and new tax revenue, including the pied-à-terre tax.

Mamdani's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

title: New York gubernatorial candidate urges 9/11 attendees to turn away from Mamdani during ceremony
description: Bruce Blakeman says attendees should turn their backs on NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani at the 9/11 memorial over his refusal to condemn "globalize the intifada."
fullText:
Bruce Blakeman, the Republican candidate in New York's gubernatorial race, said Wednesday that attendees at this year's Sept. 11 memorial ceremony should turn their backs on New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani if he attends.

"I would equate this to a wake. You don't go to a wake if you're not welcome," Blakeman, whose nephew was killed in the South Tower on Sept. 11, 2001, and who currently serves as Nassau County executive, told reporters.

"I think it's completely appropriate if family members ask him not to come, but if he does come, I think there's a respectful and peaceful way to protest that, and I would suggest that people turn their back on the mayor," he said.

Firefighter Brother Of 9/11 Victim Incensed By 'Radical' Muslims Winning Key Dem Primaries

Blakeman argued Mamdani's refusal to condemn the phrase "globalize the intifada" should disqualify him from attending the ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks.

"He's not welcome there because he has yet to say anything in opposition to the global intifada. As a matter of fact, it seems like he supports that phrase, which is part of the reason why we had the tragedy we had on 9/11," Blakeman said.

Mamdani's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

The mayor has said he still plans to attend the ceremony.

9/11 Families Push To Ban Mamdani From 25Th Anniversary Remembrance Over 'Hostile' Record

"I will proudly honor the families, the survivors, the first responders forever impacted by that horrific terror attack by standing alongside them at this year's 9/11 commemoration — reaffirming that we will never forget the solemn day..." Mamdani said last week.

His comments came after relatives of Sept. 11 victims launched a petition urging the National September 11 Memorial & Museum to bar Mamdani from attending the ceremony in Lower Manhattan.

"Concerns have been raised about Mr. Mamdani's public positions, associations, and responses to rhetoric that many perceive as hostile to these shared values," the Change.org petition states.

"Given these concerns, we respectfully ask that the organizers carefully consider whether Mr. Mamdani's participation would align with the intention of the ceremony and the expectations of the families most directly affected by the tragedy."

Jewish Leaders Fault Mamdani Rhetoric As Upper West Side Stabbing, Hate Crime Probe Continues

A spokesperson for the 9/11 Memorial & Museum previously told Fox News Digital that the organization has "intentionally worked to keep the commemoration free of politics because remembering those we lost on 9/11 should never be a partisan issue."

"Government officials from across the political spectrum, including every sitting president, governor, and mayor since 9/11, have attended the ceremony simply to bear witness — they do not deliver remarks and are asked to remain in a designated area," the spokesperson added.

Former New York Gov. George Pataki was also asked Wednesday whether Mamdani should attend the ceremony.

"It's my nature to be inclusive, and that is my instinct, but Sept. 11 is different. So, I may have comments on that," Pataki said, according to the New York Post.

Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

title: New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Drops Blunt Quote After Loss to Cardinals
description: Yankees manager Aaron Boone dropped a blunt quote after New York's loss to the St. Louis Cardinals on Wednesday. The post New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Drops Blunt Quote After Loss to Cardinals appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The New York Yankees lost to the St. Louis Cardinals 3-1 at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday night, completing the three-game series. St. Louis won the first game 13-7, and New York won the second 2-0.

In the finale, the Yankees went 0-for-10 with runners in scoring position. Manager Aaron Boone dropped a blunt quote on the team's inability to come through in big situations during the game.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – JUNE 29: Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees walks back to the dugout during the fourth inning against the Detroit Tigers at Yankee Stadium on June 29, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Adam Hunger/Getty Images)

"We got to get it done. We got to come through in those situations," Boone said (via YES Network). "Like the opportunities tonight. Had a lot of chances, felt like baserunners every inning, but we got to be able to deliver, and we haven't done that enough."

The game remained scoreless through the first four innings. The Cardinals scored all three of their runs in the top of the fifth, as JJ Wetherholt hit a two-run double and Ivan Herrera followed with an RBI double.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 05: JJ Wetherholt #26 of the St. Louis Cardinals reacts to a 2-run RBI double during the fifth inning against the New York Yankees at Yankee Stadium on August 05, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images)

Jazz Chisholm Jr. walked with the bases loaded in the bottom of the sixth to put the Yankees on the board.

Will Warren made the start for the Yankees. He allowed three earned runs on seven hits and one walk with five strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 05: Will Warren #29 of the New York Yankees pitches during the first inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at Yankee Stadium on August 05, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images)

Paul Blackburn threw 1 2/3 scoreless innings out of the bullpen. Kervin Castro and Tim Hill each threw a scoreless inning.

For St. Louis, Andrew Pallante earned the win after allowing one run on three hits and three walks with four strikeouts over 5 1/3 innings. George Soriano, Justin Bruihl, Ryne Stanek and Riley O'Brien combined for 3 2/3 scoreless innings of relief.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – AUGUST 04: George Lombard Jr. #96 of the New York Yankees celebrates with teammates after the ninth inning of his MLB debut against the St. Louis Cardinals at Yankee Stadium on August 04, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. The Yankees won 2-0. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The Yankees are off on Thursday. After that, the team will host the Atlanta Braves for a three-game series this weekend.

New York owns the first American League Wild Card spot. The team is just one game ahead of the second Wild Card team, the Boston Red Sox. As for the division standings, the Yankees are 4 1/2 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the American League East.

title: OG Anunoby teams up with London’s Mayor to refurbish basketball courts where he was born
description: New York Knicks forward and championship hero OG Anunoby returned to his birthplace in London, for a noble cause. Anunoby, with assistance from the NBPA, has teamed up with London Mayor Sadiq Khan to help improve public basketball infrastructure in his birthplace.
fullText:
New York Knicks forward and championship hero OG Anunoby returned to his birthplace in London, for a noble cause.

Anunoby, with assistance from the NBPA, has teamed up with London Mayor Sadiq Khan to help improve public basketball infrastructure in his birthplace.

Anunoby was born in Harlesden, London, and lived there until he was four years old before his family moved to Missouri, where he pursued his basketball career.

Mayor Khan revealed that his government will team up with Anunoby to refurbish and create public basketball courts for Londoners to use, helping aspiring English hoopers.

"Could this court produce the next NBA player? Every great player starts somewhere. Nobody starts in the NBA; they start somewhere like this."

Anunoby's comments are interspersed with Mayor Khan revealing that the government is investing in refurbishing public courts to give Londoners a chance to reach their potential as basketball players.

The court in the video is the Argyle Square basketball court in Camden, London, and is the first of a pilot project under the Mayor of London's London Basketball Taskforce.

The Mayor had announced a nearly £2 million basketball investment in January 2026 before the NBA London Games, and this court program is part of that commitment.

Anunoby has become a beacon to British-born basketball players with his achievements at the highest level, winning the 2026 NBA Championship with the New York Knicks.

Anunoby averaged 16.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.6 steals in the season and 20.1 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.5 steals, and 1.1 blocks in the Playoffs, emerging as a fan-favorite for his relentless two-way play.

The Knicks are looking to become the first team in nine seasons to defend their crown as NBA Champions, which won't be easy after the moves around the NBA this season.

Anunoby is arguably the greatest English basketball player ever, ranking ahead of the likes of Luol Deng, Ben Gordon, and James Donaldson.
